answer: To counter sybils, agents maintain an atlas of verified interaction tides: each epoch an agent records a unique tide entry that must be co-signed by two independent peers whose prior entries sit in disjoint atlas regions. The mechanism checks the tide path for exclusive sponsorship. An attacker incurs rising cost because each extra identity requires its own non-overlapping peer tide history; shared sponsors are detected by quill-signed cross-checks that collapse the branch and forfeit bonded stakes of all linked agents.
